subject: [Merging ggmap maps] 3 equal size/scale/zoom maps show different margins once merged

messages.author: 3e0789c3e81cef70
messages.subject: [Merging ggmap maps] 3 equal size/scale/zoom maps show different margins once merged
parts:
Hi there!,

Is there any way of fixing the plot-area size of -ggmap- function as after trying to merge two or more maps?. I have three graphs (maps) that have the same scale, zoom and geo-dimentions, i.e. all three of them were downloaded from OSM, using scale = OSM_scale_lookup(zoom = 7) and the same bounding box sizes, the only diference is on latitude coordinates, these follow:

Map1:
 left bottom  right    top 
 -75    -29    -65    -16

Map2:
 left bottom  right    top 
 -75    -42    -65    -29 

Map3:
 left bottom  right    top 
 -75    -55    -65    -42

Please note that abs(top - bottom) always equals 13, thus, considering that the three maps should have the same dimentions, I was hoping that once I merge them into a single device they all keep the same width and height (and that is where my problem lies). The code I'm using to generate this:

# left, bottom, right, top
b.box <- c(left=-75, bottom=-55, right=-65, top=-16)

# Setting boxes
tamano <- abs(b.box["top"] - b.box["bottom"])/3
b.box1 <- b.box2 <- b.box3 <- b.box
b.box1["bottom"] <- b.box1["top"] - tamano

b.box2["top"] <- b.box1["bottom"]
b.box2["bottom"] <- b.box1["bottom"] - tamano

b.box3["top"] <- b.box2["bottom"]
b.box3["bottom"] <- b.box2["bottom"] - tamano

mymap1 <- get_map(b.box1,source="osm",scale=OSM_scale_lookup(zoom =7), color="bw")
mymap2 <- get_map(b.box2,source="osm",scale=OSM_scale_lookup(zoom =7), color="bw")
mymap3 <- get_map(b.box3,source="osm",scale=OSM_scale_lookup(zoom =7), color="bw")

map1 <- ggmap(mymap1,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Norte") 
map2 <- ggmap(mymap2,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Centro") 
map3 <- ggmap(mymap3,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Sur") 

# Merging
gridExtra::grid.arrange(map1, map2,map3, ncol=3)

Please note that abs(top - bottom) always equals 13, thus, considering that the three maps should have the same dimentions, I was hoping that once I merge them into a single device they all keep the same width and height (and that is where my problem lies). I have attached a picture of what I'm getting as a result after merging the three maps.

Thanks in advanced!

George

messages.subject: Re: [Merging ggmap maps] 3 equal size/scale/zoom maps show different margins once merged
parts:
Hi Brandon!

Thanks for the reply. Just like you, I'm having trouble to get access to OSM, so I've switched to google. Either way, I'm still getting the same problem. As google does not support bouding box, I'm trimming the maps on my own using scale_x_continuous(). The example follows (with the new result attached):

library(ggmap)
library(gridExtra)
rm(list=ls())

b.box <- c(left=-75, bottom=-55, right=-65, top=-16)

# Setting boxes
tamano <- abs(b.box["top"] - b.box["bottom"])/3
b.box1 <- b.box2 <- b.box3 <- b.box
b.box1["bottom"] <- b.box1["top"] - tamano

b.box2["top"] <- b.box1["bottom"]
b.box2["bottom"] <- b.box1["bottom"] - tamano

b.box3["top"] <- b.box2["bottom"]
b.box3["bottom"] <- b.box2["bottom"] - tamano

# Getting the centre coordinates
centre <- function(x) c(lon=(x["right"]+x["left"])/2,lat=(x["top"]+x["bottom"])/2)

mymap1 <- get_map(centre(b.box1),source="google",zoom=4, color="bw")
mymap2 <- get_map(centre(b.box2),source="google",zoom=4, color="bw")
mymap3 <- get_map(centre(b.box3),source="google",zoom=4, color="bw")

map1 <- ggmap(mymap1,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Norte") + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits=b.box1[c("left","right")]) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=b.box1[c("bottom","top")])

map2 <- ggmap(mymap2,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Centro") + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits=b.box2[c("left","right")]) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=b.box2[c("bottom","top")])

map3 <- ggmap(mymap3,extent="normal") + labs(title="Zona Sur") + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits=b.box3[c("left","right")]) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=b.box3[c("bottom","top")])

# Merging
gridExtra::grid.arrange(map1, map2,map3, ncol=3)
Thanks!

George, 

I can confirm that the issue is replicated on my machine. Without your scales though, the plots do match up, which suggests that the problem is there, but I don't use ggmap enough to really know for sure. 

If I had to guess, and I will, I would guess that the difference is that it's the projection method. The further south you go, the map begins to stretch a bit and that's why the tip of Chile and Argentina are really long compared with the northern parts. But, that's a guess. 

B

messages.subject: Re: [Merging ggmap maps] 3 equal size/scale/zoom maps show different margins once merged
parts:
Hey Brandon, George –

Looking briefly into the problem, it looks like you can get what you want, George, with a simple change to ggmap:::stitch.  (You just need to remove the lines order <- ... and the next one, tiles <- tiles[order].

Actually, the question helped me to realize a change in some Stamen maps stuff.  If you install the dev version I just pushed to github, you can get what you want all in one go (I think) :

install_github("ggmap", "dkahle")
library(ggmap)

# left, bottom, right, top
b.box <- c(left=-75, bottom=-55, right=-65, top=-16)

ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 5, maptype = "toner"), extent = "device")
ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 5, maptype = "toner-lite"), extent = "device")

b.box <- c(left=-80, bottom=-55, right=-60, top=-16)
ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 5, maptype = "toner"), extent = "device")
ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 5, maptype = "toner-lite"), extent = "device")

b.box <- c(left=-80, bottom=-55, right=-60, top=-16)
ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 6, maptype = "toner"), extent = "device")
ggmap(get_stamenmap(b.box, zoom = 6, maptype = "toner-lite"), extent = "device")


Note that not all the Stamen maps cover the entire globe.

Cheers
david.

Oh!  Yes, that's right.  I'm sorry, due to some off-list messages I misinterpreted the problem.

But that's right, as you go further south (north) in the mercator the sizes of maps will stretch vertically.

I don't see a way around the problem.  If you want to force it, you can remove the map scale as below, but (of course) that'll change things...

Best
david.

b.box1 <- b.box2 <- b.box3 <- b.box
b.box1["bottom"] <- b.box1["top"] - tamano

b.box2["top"] <- b.box1["bottom"]
b.box2["bottom"] <- b.box1["bottom"] - tamano

b.box3["top"] <- b.box2["bottom"]
b.box3["bottom"] <- b.box2["bottom"] - tamano

mymap1 <- get_stamenmap(b.box1, 7, "toner", color="bw")
mymap2 <- get_stamenmap(b.box2, 7, "toner", color="bw")
mymap3 <- get_stamenmap(b.box3, 7, "toner", color="bw")

map1 <- ggmap(mymap1,extent="device") + ggtitle("Zona Norte") 
map2 <- ggmap(mymap2,extent="device") + ggtitle("Zona Centro") 
map3 <- ggmap(mymap3,extent="device") + ggtitle("Zona Sur")

grid.arrange(
  map1 + coord_cartesian(), 
  map2 + coord_cartesian(), 
  map3 + coord_cartesian(), 
  ncol = 3
)
